title: Gemma 4 E2B/E4B fine-tuning, adapters, and adaptation closure
question: Which fine-tuning and adaptation paths, target-surface constraints, quality and retention trade-offs, and deployment or MTP couplings are repeatedly evidenced for Gemma 4 E2B and E4B, and which remain framework-, revision-, task-, or artifact-bound?

inclusion_criteria: Official Gemma 4 tuning guidance or an exact runnable E2B/E4B recipe.
Independent controlled study with method, configuration, and measured adaptation outcomes.
Inspectably retained adapter, commit-pinned implementation, or exact failure report that constrains training, merge, export, or serving.
Evidence that preserves adaptation method, module or tower scope, library revision, denominator, evaluation boundary, and temporal state.
exclusion_criteria: Generic LoRA guidance without a Gemma 4 binding.
Unversioned VRAM or quality claims lacking configuration and denominator.
Training loss or a tutorial sample treated as accepted held-out capability evidence.
Dependent restatements counted as independent corroboration.
Issue closure treated as technical resolution without a linked change or rerun.

generality_probe.rationale: The pass compares materially different adaptation methods and acceptance surfaces rather than inferring a family-wide rule from one provider tutorial or task.

clusters.label: MTP performance after adaptation belongs to the target/drafter pair
clusters.supported_scope: Google documents architectural coupling and NVIDIA supplies a concrete joint E4B training and throughput route, supporting paired versioning and evaluation when MTP is required.
transfer_limits: The only retained post-tuning result is one provider's full-joint E4B experiment over 20 prompts.
unresolved_configuration_gaps: LoRA-specific, E2B, batch, hardware, and domain-shift acceptance measurements are absent.
clusters.next_action: Measure target/drafter acceptance before and after the intended adaptation instead of inheriting base-checkpoint speed claims.

tensions.label: Multimodal dataset versus trainable modality tower
tensions.analysis: The sources are compatible after splitting input modality from parameter scope: official image-conditioned QLoRA can train only the LM, while specialized selectors can adapt wrapped audio or vision components.
tensions.remaining_question: When does tower adaptation improve held-out modality behavior enough to justify its portability and retention risk?

tensions.label: Documented merge path versus runtime-specific checkpoint divergence
tensions.analysis: Google and PEFT describe valid base-plus-adapter and merge paths within their stack; MLX shows that a different conversion and runtime pair can still disagree structurally. Portability is therefore a separate acceptance axis.
tensions.remaining_question: Which exact export and serving routes are required by the owner realization?

tensions.label: Target-task gain versus orthogonal capability loss
tensions.analysis: The tension is real rather than contradictory: the same adaptation can improve a target distribution while degrading other capabilities, and controls move both sides differently.
tensions.remaining_question: Which target and retention endpoints define acceptable AoA utility for each adaptation role?

tensions.label: E2B operational accessibility versus E4B controlled evidence depth
tensions.analysis: The corpus is asymmetric: E2B has accessible recipes and an artifact, while E4B has stronger controlled outcome studies. Cross-source resource or quality ranking would mix methods and instruments.
tensions.remaining_question: How do E2B and E4B compare under one fixed stack, dataset, token budget, target surface, task suite, and deployment path?

method_pressures.pressure: A label such as LoRA or QLoRA hides the base revision, quantization, tower scope, wrapper depth, chat template, loss mask, special-token behavior, and library fix state that determine whether two runs are comparable.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Require an adaptation manifest that records exact base and processor revisions, method, quantization, fully qualified target selectors by tower, modules_to_save, weight tying, template/thinking/loss-mask contract, sequence and optimizer controls, and dependency lock.

method_pressures.pressure: Training completion, task quality, retained capability, adapter reload, merge, export, real serving, and MTP throughput are different claims but web reports frequently collapse them.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Preserve an ordered but non-substitutive acceptance ladder: numeric training health, held-out target behavior, orthogonal and safety probes, reload, merge/unmerge, export, target-runtime serving, and optional target/drafter acceptance.

method_pressures.pressure: Independent QLoRA and CPT studies show that a successful specialization result can conceal general-capability erosion and that adapter rank, learning rate, and mixture alter the frontier.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Do not admit an adaptation study from training loss or target metrics alone; require a role-relevant target suite, orthogonal retention suite, safety/boundary cases, failure cases, and explicit checkpoint-selection rule.

method_pressures.pressure: The web corpus cannot separate model-size effects from method, data, hardware, runtime, rank, and evaluation differences across E2B and E4B adaptation reports.
method_pressures.proposed_response: Run a bounded owner study holding stack, data, token budget, target surface, quantization, rank, sequence, optimizer, checkpoint rule, task graders, retention suite, and deployment acceptance constant across E2B and E4B.

revisit_triggers: A same-instrument E2B/E4B adaptation benchmark with retained artifacts is published or run by the owner.
A released PEFT regression matrix establishes wrapped vision/audio tower train, merge, and export behavior.
An independent Gemma 4 multimodal adapter study reports target quality, text and modality retention, and portable serving.
The MLX Python/Swift fused-checkpoint round trip is resolved by a linked patch and reproducible test.
A LoRA-specific study measures Gemma 4 target/drafter acceptance before and after adaptation.
A long-context Gemma 4 adaptation run approaches 128K with both training and serving evidence.
Any mutable official recipe, upstream issue, or commit-pinned notebook changes its dependency, target-surface, or closure state.
